comparability.within_group: All rows are reported together by DreamGaussian4D on the same Consistent4D novel-view benchmark. This review transcribes reported results; it does not rerun or harmonize the implementations.
comparability.configuration_difference: Fast uses 16 rather than 32 frames and fewer random views, so label it explicitly as a speed configuration, not an independently ranked method.
comparability.hardware: DreamGaussian4D reports a single 80 GB A100 for its experiments (p.6). Baseline timing hardware is not separately specified; do not assume every time entry used that same GPU.
comparability.do_not_mix: The 6.5-min/14-frame image-to-4D result in Table 1 is a different task and configuration from the 15-min/32-frame video-to-4D result in Table 3.
comparability.missing: Exact evaluation image resolution, per-baseline checkpoint details, FVD feature/preprocessing configuration, seeds and uncertainty are not reported in the inspected sections.

groups.suggested_caption: Reported video-to-4D results on seven Consistent4D videos (32 frames, four novel views). Fast uses 16 frames and one random optimization view; the full DreamGaussian4D setting uses 32 frames and four views. Runtime denotes offline content generation.

groups.title: Camera control and revisit consistency in world generation
groups.task: Camera-conditioned video generation under short trajectories and longer out-and-back trajectories.

protocol.dataset: Author-constructed mixed test suite: DL3DV, game videos, and AI-generated images
protocol.test_size: 600 cases overall; component counts and separate short/long counts NR
protocol.short_reference: Generated frames versus ground-truth frames from test videos.
protocol.long_reference: Frames on the return path versus corresponding frames generated on the initial pass; a self-revisit consistency test.
protocol.conditions: Camera trajectories/poses supplied to every model; WorldPlay converts poses to discrete actions when only poses are given. The test suite includes image-conditioned cases.
protocol.resolution: WorldPlay operating point is 720p. The paper does not state a uniform evaluation resolution or resizing policy for all methods in Table 2.
protocol.pose_evaluation: ViPE estimates generated camera poses; both trajectories are made relative to the first frame and translation scale is normalized using the furthest frame.

metrics.definition: arccos((trace(R_gen R_gt^T)-1)/2), Eq.(6). Do not label the reported numbers as degrees without an explicit source statement.

metrics.label: T_dist
metrics.unit: normalized squared translation distance; not metres

Full Context Forcing-distilled autoregressive model: 4 denoising steps; 4 latent frames per chunk; 3 temporal-memory chunks, 1 spatial-memory chunk, plus first-chunk attention sink. Pretrained DiT video backbone cited as Wan/HunyuanVideo; exact checkpoint size not resolved by this paper's Appendix A.

comparability.within_group: One author-run comparison table and one described test suite; short and long blocks have different reference targets and must remain separately labelled.
comparability.do_not_pool: Long-term PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS quantify revisit consistency with the initial generated pass, not fidelity to observed ground truth. They cannot be averaged with short-term scores or treated as the same reconstruction metric.
comparability.excluded_row: Ours (w/o Context Forcing) is an ablation and is excluded from the full-method comparison.
comparability.configuration_gaps: The inspected paper names baselines but does not enumerate exact checkpoints, sampling steps, common resizing or per-method compute budgets for every row.
comparability.source_issue: The VMem row's citation is printed as Wang et al. (2024b), whereas the table caption and baseline paragraph identify Li et al. (2025b). Preserve the numerical row under VMem and cite WorldPlay as measurement source; do not reproduce the inconsistent row citation.

efficiency_separate_note.meaning: Generation/streaming throughput with parallelism, quantization and streaming decoding; not an end-to-end action-to-display latency measurement.
efficiency_separate_note.do_not_convert: Do not invert FPS and report it as measured interaction latency.

groups.suggested_caption: WorldPlay-reported camera-controlled generation on a 600-case mixed test suite. Short-term scores (61 frames) use observed reference frames; long-term scores (at least 250 frames) compare revisits with the initial generated pass. Pose errors use ViPE and normalized relative trajectories.

groups.title: Opponent-presence consistency in two-player generation
groups.task: Generate synchronized player observations while sharing one level/state.

protocol.dataset: ViZDoom/Doom multiplayer trajectories; the multiplayer study uses one map.
protocol.test_size: NR: random multiplayer trajectories are sampled, but the number is not given.
protocol.video_length: T steps; numerical T is NR for Table 2.
protocol.conditions: Same ground-truth per-player action streams; each method generates paired Player 1/Player 2 views. Shared map/state information is supplied according to the method's conditioning design.
protocol.reference: Presence judgment on corresponding ground-truth frames, rather than direct geometric overlap.
protocol.judge: Pretrained VLM, cited to the OpenAI o1 system card; exact deployed judge model/version/prompt NR.
protocol.metrics_evaluation: Per timestep and player, ask the VLM whether the opponent is present; compare the generated-frame judgment with the judgment on the matching ground-truth frame.

rows.configuration: External-state conditioning baseline; evaluated on the same forced action trajectories. Exact checkpoint and training settings NR.
External-state conditioning baseline; evaluated on the same forced action trajectories. Exact checkpoint and training settings NR.

Two-player split-screen diffusion baseline, jointly predicts both views on the same map without explicit external memory. This is the MultiGen paper's evaluated baseline, not a verified public product checkpoint.

Separate per-player Observation/Dynamics instances with shared static map and active player poses; local frame history, action and memory-derived readouts condition each observation. Exact main-table context length and sampling steps NR.

comparability.within_group: All four rows are the authors' paired-player rollout comparison under forced ground-truth actions and the same VLM presence judge.
comparability.supported_claim: Opponent appearance/disappearance consistency across player views.
comparability.not_measured: These numbers do not measure exact object geometry, stereo consistency, physical collision correctness, or action-to-display latency.
comparability.configuration_gaps: Test trajectory count, rollout T, resolution, exact VLM checkpoint/prompt, baseline training budgets and seeds are not specified in the inspected paper.
comparability.no_inferred_sample_size: Do not mistake the >10-million-frame training collection for the evaluation sample count.

groups.suggested_caption: Reported two-player opponent-presence consistency in MultiGen. A VLM evaluates generated and corresponding ground-truth frames under matched action streams; opponent-visible is the positive class. Test trajectory count, rollout length and frame resolution are not reported.
